# Sources

**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Run:** ultradeep deep-research, subject `app-dev`

Full source registry for this run. Every `[Sn]` cited anywhere in this subject directory resolves here.
`FETCHED` means a real page retrieval produced the quote in `ledger/evidence.jsonl`. `UNREACHABLE` and
`SEARCH-ONLY` sources are listed for transparency and are **not** used to support any claim stated as fact
in the body of `REPORT.md`; where their content mattered it is named in `GAPS.md` instead.

Quality tiers: `primary` (papers, standards, official leaderboards, the thing itself) ·
`vendor-primary` (a vendor's own docs, authoritative for its own syntax/pricing only) ·
`vendor` (vendor marketing/blog) · `secondary` (reputable press, independent analysts) ·
`blog` (practitioner/agency/community) · `aggregator` (low-quality SEO compilation).

## Conflicts between sources

| Conflict | Sources | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified top score: 76.80% vs 83.5% vs 95–97% | S2 (standardized harness) · S3 (Epoch independent) · S26 and other aggregators (vendor self-reports) | Not resolved in favour of one number. The divergence is itself the finding, mechanism given by S4 and S19 (scaffold dependence). `REPORT.md` cites S2 and S3 only and names the aggregator figures as unverified. See `REPORT.md` Limitations. |
| Whether separate-tester benefits extend to weaker models | previously recorded as a conflict on the strength of a misquotation of S66 | **Resolved, and the conflict was spurious.** S66's abstract states "replacing unreliable feedback with a stronger tester restores positive gains for a lower-capability backbone" — i.e. a stronger tester *helps* a weaker backbone. The supposed contradicting quote did not exist. |
| Coverage-type equivalence for LLM-generated suites | S58 (Inozemtseva, peer-reviewed) vs a 2026 replicability study reported by `r-test` as contradicting it for LLM-generated tests (not fetched) | The 2014 result is cited only for the general claim; the LLM-specific transfer is listed in `GAPS.md`. |
| Whether multi-agent decomposition helps coding | S101 (+90.2% on a *research* eval) vs S101's own caveat and S102 | Resolved against multi-agent code-writing: both sources agree coding is a poor fit. The 90.2% figure is never applied to coding in this report. |
| Self-refinement gain magnitude | S113 (~20% absolute, 2023) vs S114 (peak +7.1 pts, 2026) | Reported as shrinking/contested; the older headline is not used. |
